title: Functions, methods & interfaces
course_section: Functions in the go programming language

hints.TestVariadic: Inside Sum, nums is a []int: range over it. SumSlice just returns Sum(xi...).
hints.TestDefer: Use a NAMED result (log []string). Deferred funcs can modify it after the return: defer func() { log = append(log, "one") }() ... then append "body" and return log.
hints.TestMethods: fmt.Sprintf("I am %s and I am %d years old", p.First, p.Age)
hints.TestStringer: fmt.Sprintf("%s (%d)", p.First, p.Age). Don't call fmt.Sprint(p) inside String(): that recurses forever!
hints.TestInterfaces: Square: s.Length * s.Width. Circle: math.Pi * math.Pow(c.Radius, 2). Info: fmt.Sprintf("area: %.2f", s.Area())
hints.TestWriter: _, err := w.Write([]byte("Hello, " + name + "!\n")); return err  (or fmt.Fprintf(w, ...))
hints.TestMockDB: u, err := ds.GetUser(id); if err != nil { return "", fmt.Errorf("greet: %w", err) }; return "Hello, " + u.Name, nil
hints.TestCallback: fmt.Sprintf("the square of %d is %d", n, f(n))
hints.TestClosure: n := 0; return func() int { n++; return n }
hints.TestRecursion: if n <= 1 { return 1 }; return n * Factorial(n-1)

quiz.q: In what order do these print? defer fmt.Print(1); defer fmt.Print(2); fmt.Print(3)
quiz.why: 3 prints first, then deferred calls run LIFO: 2, then 1.

quiz.q: How does a type implement an interface in Go?
options: implicitly, by having all its methods

quiz.q: How do you pass xs := []int{1,2} to func sum(n ...int)?
quiz.why: The ... after the slice unfurls it.

options: a func that closes a file
a func value that captures variables from its enclosing scope
quiz.why: The inner func keeps access to outer variables even after the outer func returns.

quiz.q: Which interface does a type satisfy to control how fmt.Println prints it?

options: by value for ints, by reference for structs
quiz.why: Everything in Go is pass by value. Pointers and slice headers are values too.
